route: exempt (data_labels) + corroboration: source-codebook code->text tie, independent second codebook (psychTools::spi.dictionary), official SPI-135 form printing code beside item and beside the 1..6 numbering, and a response-direction check (route 8)
evidence: Every item is distinguished from every other by its own code: the IRW item codes are the raw q_### column names of the SAPA deposits (data/condon_2024_sapa_personality.py renames nothing), and ItemInfo.csv in doi:10.7910/DVN/3BTT82 maps each of those 135 codes to its text directly -- 135/135 exact set match against the live table, 0 text mismatches on re-fetch. Two independent sources reproduce the same 135 code->text ties: psychTools::spi.dictionary (135/135 agreement, differing only by stripped apostrophes/quotes) and the SPI-135-27&5 v1.2 form PDF (135/135 codes, 4 trivial punctuation/wording differences listed in provenance). No positional or order inference anywhere. option_text<->resp: the form prints 1..6 under Very Inaccurate..Very Accurate; the live data agrees in direction -- 'Cheat to get ahead.' 2.20, 'Use others for my own ends.' 2.46, 'Tell a lot of lies.' 2.64 vs 'Am concerned about others.' 4.83, 'Feel sympathy for those who are worse off than myself.' 4.85, 'Sympathize with others' feelings.' 4.86, a 2.19-point separation that inverts under a flipped key. Per-item n ranges 433,019-555,453 (ratio 1.28), consistent with SAPA's planned-missing administration and showing no item conflating two questions; all 135 items span all six levels. What this does NOT establish: the wording of the four intermediate anchors is taken from the official form rather than re-derived from the data, The item/resp gate itself is settled and is no longer part of this hedge: it was reproduced server-side against Redivis during the round, and re-confirmed by audit_batch.R on 2026-08-24 (item set 135/135, resp 1-6).

route: Reconstruction of scored accuracy from the study's raw per-option data + SI answer key, compared to live per-item means (SKILL.md Step 5b routes 1 and 9), plus within-question order concordance
evidence: Route: reconstruct each item's scored accuracy from the study's own raw per-option endorsement file (OSF pyb8s compiled.csv, 680,333 respondents, one 0/1 column per option) using the SI answer key under the claimed letter->index mapping (a=1 ... h=8), and compare with the live per-item mean over 1,131,401 respondents (Redivis aggregate; irw_fetch pulls 107,483,095 rows and is unreliable). All 95 items reproduce: cor = 0.9812, mean|diff| = 0.0203, max|diff| = 0.0785 (largest: q34_1 0.820 vs live 0.742; q34_6 0.858 vs 0.786; q24_4 0.902 vs 0.832), and all diffs bar two are positive, i.e. a uniform sample-composition offset rather than item-specific error. Reading ANY single item's key the other way would move it by at least 0.4859 (median ~0.93), so all 95 Correct/Incorrect class assignments are pinned outright. Permutation null for the correlation: mean 0.001, max 0.353 over 2,000 draws, vs 0.9812 observed. Within-question option ORDER (immune to the sample offset) is concordant on 113 of 120 pairs; the 7 discordant pairs are all near-ties (|diff in live| 0.0031-0.0184) and 3 of them are still separated by keyed class. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: 4 pairs -- q17_1/q17_3, q20_1/q20_3, q24_1/q24_3, q26_2/q26_4 -- share a keyed class AND order discordantly, so their own numbers do not distinguish them from each other; they rest on the single global letter->index convention (validated by the other 113 orderings and all 95 class assignments), not on item-specific evidence. Hence PARTIAL. Separately, q10_4 is assigned to the fourth printed option because the SI prints Question 10's options as a, b, c, c; the recomputed accuracy 0.9987 vs live 0.9975 is consistent but, both q10 items being keyed Incorrect and both near ceiling, does not by itself exclude the alternative reading.

evidence: Item axis: every one of the 11 IRW codes is the deposited Stata variable name minus its exam suffix (data/ftna_kasper_2022.r: gsub('_ftna','')/gsub('_psle','')), so each item is distinguished from every other by name identity rather than inference. Confirmed structurally against the live data: the study's do-file names the PSLE subject set as {kiswahili, english, math, society, science} and the live table has exactly those 5 items at wave 0 and exactly the 9 FTNA subjects at wave 1 (633,038 respondents in each of the 14 item-wave cells). Resp axis: edcc_code/taba7_taba8.do recodes _num 0/1/2/3/4 to NECTA points 5/15.5/25.5/35.5/45.5 and bands them E/D/C/B/A, and edcc_code/tab2_fig1_figa1_taba1.do independently relabels the ascending value groups E,D,C,B,A -- each of the 5 levels pinned twice. Direction confirmed in the data: private-school students score +1.265 higher than public at FTNA (2.24 vs 0.97) and +0.433 higher at PSLE (2.61 vs 2.18), matching Brandt's positive private premium; and FTNA subject means run math 0.47 < physics 0.51 < chemistry 0.87 < geography 0.97 < history 1.05 < biology 1.11 < civics 1.47 < english 1.66 < kiswahili 1.81, i.e. mathematics worst and Kiswahili best, as expected when 4=A.

route: 1 (published per-item statistics) + 8 (semantic coherence of the response distribution, via image-derived rotation angle)
evidence: Route B (published per-item stats): paper Supplementary Table S7 lists mean and N for 58 items keyed by the live q_16NNN codes. All 58 live row counts equal the published N EXACTLY (e.g. q_16104 23106/23106, q_16026 23839/23839) and live proportion correct matches the published mean to <=0.005 (S7 is rounded to 2dp) with r=0.9999 over the 58 -- which also fixes the option axis: resp==1 is the correct response (q_16104 lives at 0.123 correct, the paper's hardest item at .12). Structural: exactly 70 items have n>10000 and that set is exactly S7's 58 plus the 12 items the study's code drops, i.e. the paper's 70-item final pool; the other 234 pilot items sit at a median n of 1224. Route A (stimulus images -> data): the target rotation of each of the 304 PNGs was recovered mechanically (Jaccard of the right panel's white pixels against the four rotations of the left panel; 78 at 0deg / 84 at 90 / 73 at 180 / 69 at 270). All 12 items the study's Rmd drops as 'not requiring mental rotation' come out 0deg (12/12; 0deg figures are 25.7% of the pool, so p=8.1e-08 under a permuted fig<->item pairing), and 0deg items average p(correct)=0.555 vs 0.378 for rotated ones (Welch t=9.1, p=2e-15). PARTIAL not VERIFIED: the 304 figures contain only 111 distinct stimulus:target panels (many items reuse a panel and differ only in their answer options), so Route A cannot separate two items sharing a panel, and Route B covers 58 of 304 items. The fig<->item tie rests on the filename convention, corroborated item-wise only for q_16104 (the Rmd displays fig16104.png as that item).
